title: TRIAGE: Dialectical LLM Reasoning for Explainable Risk Prediction on Irregularly Sampled Medical Time Series
abstract: arXiv:2606.09030v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Clinical early warning systems built on irregularly sampled medical time series (ISMTS) from electronic health records must deliver continuous risk scores for patient triage as well as interpretable rationales that clinicians can verify. Large language models (LLMs) are uniquely positioned for both, deriving risk from their output probabilities and rationales from their medical knowledge. However, we find that conventional LLM reasoning collapses graded risk into overconfident predictions and thereby undermines the cross-patient comparability on which triage depends. We refer to this failure mode as risk polarization and identify two underlying behaviors: early commitment to a single outcome, and one-sided reasoning that focuses only on the evidence for that outcome. To address this, we propose TRIAGE, a framework that trains an LLM to reason dialectically over competing clinical outcomes by eliciting outcome-specific rationale

translated_title: TRIAGE：面向不规则采样医学时间序列上可解释风险预测的辩证式大语言模型推理
translated_abstract: 基于电子健康记录中不规则采样医学时间序列（ISMTS）构建的临床早期预警系统，必须为患者分诊提供连续的风险评分，以及可供临床医生核验的可解释推理依据。大语言模型（LLM）在这两方面均具备独特优势：既能从其输出概率中推导风险，又能从其医学知识中生成推理依据。然而，我们发现传统的LLM推理会将分级的风险坍缩为过度自信的预测，从而破坏了分诊所依赖的患者间可比性。我们将这种失败模式称为“风险极化”，并识别出其背后的两种行为：过早地锁定单一结局，以及仅关注支持该结局证据的单边推理。为解决这一问题，我们提出了TRIAGE，一个训练LLM针对相互竞争的临床结局进行辩证推理的框架，通过引导模型生成针对特定结局的推理依据……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文提出TRIAGE框架，通过训练大语言模型对相互竞争的临床结局进行辩证推理，克服传统LLM推理中“风险极化”造成的过度自信问题，从而在不规则采样医学时间序列上实现连续、可跨患者比较且可解释的风险预测。
en_tdlr: TRIAGE trains LLMs to reason dialectically over competing clinical outcomes, mitigating the "risk polarization" failure of conventional LLM reasoning to deliver continuous, cross-patient comparable, and explainable risk predictions on irregularly sampled medical time series.
